svg.title: One request, end to end: sgit clone with a sealed key
svg.desc: Six lanes: the agent, the app, sharness.net, sharness.kms, the vault server, sharness.fs. Step 1, the agent runs sgit clone --sealed handover.png; step 2, the app checks the QR's JSON against a strict schema and passes the sealed m1 to net; step 3, net makes a one-time key E and asks the KMS to unwrap; step 4, the KMS thaws, checks the sealed message is addressed to it, signed, unexpired and the nonce new, derives the read and write keys, scrubs the vault key and returns the derived keys sealed to E, then freezes; step 5, net opens them with E and drops E, fetches packs from the vault server and decrypts; step 6, net hands plain file contents to the app; step 7, the app asks fs to write the tree and vault_key.sealed, which fs accepts only in a sealed format; step 8, the agent sees "cloned, sealed to sha256:..., expires 30 Oct", never a key.

g.text: 2 · strict JSON checks on the QR; the sealed m1
4 · to = me? signed? unexpired? nonce new?
derive read/write keys · scrub the vault key
7 · write the tree; write vault_key.sealed (= the m1): accepted, it is a sealed format
8 · "cloned, sealed to sha256:… from sha256:… (chains to root), expires 30 Oct"

svg.text: What the transcript sees: the command, the m1 (ciphertext), fingerprints, progress. Never a key. Every later command asks the KMS again, with a new E and a new nonce.
